description:
## Outcome

The exact draft assets for macOS ARM64, macOS x86-64, Linux x86-64, and Windows x86-64 pass the full non-interactive release contract and startup limits on native runners.

## Work

1. Download the exact draft assets and verify their external checksums before extraction.
2. Run `jido --version`, `--help`, `run --help`, `eval --help`, and `daemon --help` with no Erlang or Elixir on `PATH`.
3. Measure five warm runs and one cold run for help, version, first TUI frame, and runtime-ready state.
4. Require warm medians of at most 0.50 seconds for help and version, 0.50 seconds for the first frame, and 1.25 seconds for runtime ready.
5. Prove that input works during startup and one queued submission runs exactly once after ready.
6. Run one provider-free local scenario and prove exit statuses `0`, `1`, and `64`.
7. Run daemon start, health, request, clean stop, restart persistence, and no-daemon cases.
8. Test installation under paths with spaces and non-ASCII user profiles.
9. Validate metadata, notices, access controls, private runtime selection, JSONL, packaged runtime data, and artifact integrity.
10. Store target-scoped acceptance and performance evidence with the release candidate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All four targets pass the same required check list and warm startup limits.
- [ ] Tests use the final uploaded bytes, not a build directory.
- [ ] No test can find `erl`, `elixir`, or `mix` through `PATH`.
- [ ] The first frame precedes runtime-ready state on each target.
- [ ] No live provider credential or network model call is used.
- [ ] Daemon restart and shutdown evidence matches protocol and lifecycle policy.
- [ ] One required failure blocks later publication tasks.

## Tests

This task is the native acceptance suite. Also test that one corrupt candidate and one startup-regressed candidate block the matrix.

## Non-goals

Do not treat automated first-frame checks as manual TUI acceptance.
title: Pass automated packaged acceptance on the first target matrix
